During the migration to new postpaid balance calculations we noticed the following things:

# For more than 600+ companies, there are mismatches between its balance and a sum of all balance entries

*SQL*

{code:sql}SELECT
	bc.id,
	bc.balance,
	SUM(be.sum) AS sum
FROM
	business_company bc
	LEFT JOIN balance_entry be ON be.business_company_id = bc.id
GROUP BY bc.id
HAVING bc.balance != sum;{code}

# There are mismatches between results of the *old* and the *new* balance calculation algorithm

*SQL*

{noformat}SELECT
  result.business_company_id AS business_company_id,
  result.country,
  result.inflows + result.inflows_refunds - result.outflows AS postpaid_balance
FROM
  (
    SELECT
      bc.id AS business_company_id,
      bc.name AS name,
      bc.country AS country,
      bc.contact_email AS contact_email,
      bc.currency AS currency,
      (
        SELECT
          IFNULL(sum(be_subquery.sum), 0)
        FROM
          `balance_entry` be_subquery
          LEFT JOIN `adjustment` adj_subquery ON be_subquery.type = 'adjustment'
          AND be_subquery.reference_id = adj_subquery.id
        WHERE
          be_subquery.type in(
            'bank_transfer',
            'topup',
            'rebate',
            'apology_credit',
            'adjustment'
          )
          AND be_subquery.business_company_id = bc.id
          AND(
            adj_subquery.id IS NULL
            OR adj_subquery.is_hidden = 0
          )
      ) AS inflows,
      -- Refunds from open period & from not-overdue invoices should reduce total amount of debt
      (
        SELECT
          IFNULL(sum(be.sum), 0)
        FROM
          `balance_entry` be
          JOIN `claim_grouping` cg ON cg.id = be.reference_id
          JOIN `claim_refund` cr ON cr.grouping_id = cg.id
          JOIN `claim` c ON c.id = cr.claim_id
        WHERE
          be.type = 'claim_refund'
          AND be.business_company_id = bc.id
          AND cr.created > '2023-04-30 21:00:00'
          AND c.created < '2023-04-30 21:00:00'
      ) as inflows_refunds,
      (
        SELECT
          IFNULL(
            SUM(
              IFNULL(
                i_subquery.sum_with_vat_in_company_currency,
                i_subquery.sum_with_vat
              )
            ),
            0
          )
        FROM
          `invoice` i_subquery
        WHERE
          i_subquery.business_company_id = bc.id
      ) AS outflows,
      bc.city_id AS city_id
    FROM
      `business_company` bc
    WHERE
      bc.invoice_type = 'invoice'
      AND bc.ignore_timestamp < NOW()
  ) result
ORDER BY
  result.business_company_id;


-- fast
SELECT
	bc.id AS business_company_id,
	bc.balance - (
		SELECT
			IFNULL(SUM(
					CASE WHEN be.type = 'claim' THEN
						be.sum + IFNULL(cr.sum_vat, 0)
					ELSE
						be.sum
					END), 0) AS sum
		FROM
			`balance_entry` be
		LEFT JOIN `claim_refund` cr ON be.reference_id = cr.claim_id
	WHERE
		be.id > IFNULL(MAX(ar.balance_entry_end_id), 0)
		AND be.type IN('claim', 'voucher_usage')
		AND be.business_company_id = bc.id) balance
FROM
	business_company bc
	LEFT JOIN aggregated_record ar ON ar.business_company_id = bc.id
WHERE
	bc.invoice_type = 'invoice'
	AND bc.ignore_timestamp < NOW()
GROUP BY
	bc.id
HAVING postpaid_balance < 0;{noformat}

Hi [~accountid:5faa45acf7b30b006e3b121d] I have attached the screenshot from the ticket we have for RO market. Essentially SF becomes the part of the Delivery fee and this delivery fee is basically passed onto the courier. For example.

A courier needs to earn 3 euros according to the earnings model in the city. Then, we have 2 cases:

# Delivery fee = 1.5 euros, service fee = 0 euros. 1.5 euros gets sent to the courier, and we need to pay to the courier 1.5 as a marketplace fee.
# Delivery fee = 1.5 euros, service fee = 0.2 euros. In this case, 1.7 euros gets sent to the courier, and we only need to pay to the courier 1.3 euros as a marketplace fee.

So the amount of money that the courier receives as his earning doesn’t change, it just changes how he receives them. But for us, in the second case, it means that we are getting higher revenue from users.

I’ve created a [Mixpanel board|https://mixpanel.com/project/1165336/view/32804/app/boards#id=4941679] to get a high level view of how the users interact with the app and their path between the {{Where To}} and {{Confirm Category}} screens.
NB: The conversion data is done based on [Mixpanel sessions|https://help.mixpanel.com/hc/en-us/articles/115004695223-Track-Sessions#:~:text=An%20Event%20Based%20Session%20in,days%2C%20weeks%2C%20or%20months.] (not sessions as we define them); the Mixpanel sessions expire in 30 min, in theory our sessions should also expire in 30 min so the 2 metrics should overlap in most cases;

h3. The flows

h4. WhereTo->ConfirmCategory ([link|https://mixpanel.com/project/1165336/view/32804/app/flows#p85Sm6cjRcXi])

* Conversion: ~76%
* Looking at the steps a user can take after {{Where To}} it looks like some non-geo events contribute to conversion (eg: users switch to Scooter Map)
* Most users (~ 45%) click on the {{WhereTo}} button ({{Ride Hailing Cross Domain Tap}} event) as the next event
* ~18% of users choose a {{QuickDestination}} ({{Quick Address Tap}} event) as the next event

h4. SetPickup&Destination-Flow (from {{Set Pickup & Destination}} to {{Confirm Category}} [link|https://mixpanel.com/project/1165336/view/32804/app/flows#rr9NVMsY6Eze])

* Conversion: ~92%
* Zoomed in from the previous flow to users who have explicitly clicked on the {{WhereTo}} button and reached the {{Set Pickup & Destination}} event (and screen with the same name)- showing an intent to search for the destination
* On this screen users have multiple options for geo-related events:
** Click on a destination ({{Destination Suggestion Tap}} event)
** Click on the destination field ({{Destination Input Field Tap}} which by default is preselected, this event seems to be registered only for explicit taps, the users can start typing without the explicit tap)
** Click on choose on map for destination ({{Choose Destination on Map Tap}})
** Click on the pickup field ({{Pickup Input Field Tap}})
** Click on choose on map for pickup ({{Choose Pickup on Map Tap}}) 

h4. DestinationTextualSearch-Flow (from {{Set Pickup & Destination}} to {{Destination Suggestions Tap}} [link|https://mixpanel.com/project/1165336/view/32804/app/flows#report/39747095/destination-textual-search-flow/~(originDashboard~(id~4941679~title~'Search*2520Events*2520Test))])

* Conversion: ~87%
* Zoomed in from previous flow to users who have clicked on a destination
* By separating the {{Set Pickup & Destination}} event by the {{country}} property, we could see at a country level the conversion to {{Destination Suggestions Tap}}
* I have cross checked the data in this flow with the data we store in PSA for the 1st of May 2023. The PSA data is extracted [here|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/14OMHrvl5x2SYeTt97czD9plqrQyVSpCUzTZnsT57Vl8/edit#gid=1928667819]. Query used:
{noformat}SELECT
    admin_system_country.name AS "admin_system_country.name",
    SUM(CASE WHEN (geo_places_search_analytics.places_search_resolution = 'ABANDON_SEARCH') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "nr_of_abandons",
    count(*) AS "nr_of_searches"
FROM glue.geo__geo_live.places_search_analytics AS geo_places_search_analytics
         LEFT JOIN glue.ng_public.admin_system_city AS admin_system_city ON geo_places_search_analytics.city_id=admin_system_city.id
         LEFT JOIN glue.ng_public.admin_system_country AS admin_system_country ON admin_system_city.country_code=admin_system_country.code
WHERE (geo_places_search_analytics.created_day_str >= '2023-05-01' AND geo_places_search_analytics.created_day_str < '2023-05-02')
  AND (geo_places_search_analytics.places_search_type ) IN ('DROPOFF', 'PICKUP')
GROUP BY
    1
    ORDER BY 2 DESC
    LIMIT 100;{noformat}
* The data between PSA and Mixpanel does not match 1-1 (because they use different sessions)
** In Mixpanel the top 5 countries that start in the {{Set Pickup & Destination}} are: *za*(16% out of total, 11% did not convert), *az*(8%, 14% did not convert), *ng*(7.37%, 10% did not convert), *ua*(5.52%, 14.25% did not convert), followed by *py, gh, ro, pl, gb, th*
** In PSA the top 5 countries that abandon are: *za*(20% of total, 13% abandon), *ng*(10%, 12% abandon), *az*(8%, 16% abandon), *gh*(6%, 14% abandon), *th*(5%, 13%abandon), followed by *ua, py, kn, ro, pt, po, gb*

Sharing the advice as to the advance cash payments:

* *Can we expect the user to have the exact amount deducted and, if not, that it is the user who suffers the consequences, i.e. that he/she will de facto pay more?*
** In our view, it is acceptable to draw the user's attention to the fact that it may be difficult to give change, but we do not see any basis for requiring the consumer to have the amount deducted as well as charging the consumer with the consequence of paying a higher fare.
** On the one hand, there is no provision that obliges the vendor to hold the change and give the change - there have been diverging statements in the media over the years by employees of e.g. the Trade Inspection and the UOKIK as to whether it is the consumer who is obliged to pay the deducted price or whether it is the trader who is obliged to give the change. On the other hand, however, payment with a higher denomination is still payment of the price. 
** At the same time, one has to bear in mind the principles of social co-existence (Art. 354 of the Civil Code) and that refusing to accept means of payment/ giving change or intentionally paying with a significantly higher denomination may violate them. 
** For the same reasons, it would also not be appropriate under these provisions to expect the consumer to pay more for the service because the driver does not have change to give.
* *Can we expect payment of the fare in advance? Is an explicit provision in the terms and conditions required for this (in the current version we have the option to pay by various methods, but no details of when payment is taken regulations, para. 3)?*
** Yes, payment "in advance" can be used. There is no general prohibition of the "upfront" payment model with consumers.
** As a general rule, if the price for the service is clearly and concretely established before the service is provided then it would be possible to establish payment for the service in advance. In this case, at the latest at the time the consumer expresses his or her willingness to be bound by the contract, the trader has a duty to inform the consumer in a clear and comprehensible manner of the total price for the service provided. Such information should in our view appear in the terms and conditions as well as clearly in the application.
** *If an obligation to pay in advance is introduced, if the user does not have the exact amount deducted, can the driver refuse the ride (risk of driver offence?) or expect the user to pay more if the driver is not there to give change?*
** In our opinion, the driver should not refuse to fulfil the fare if the user does not have the exact amount of the fare deducted - the driver should ensure that he/she has the means on him/her to give change. Nor should the user be expected to pay more if the driver is not there to give change.
** According to Article 138 of the Code of Offences: "Whoever, when professionally engaged in the provision of services, demands and collects for the provision of services a payment higher than the applicable one, or intentionally refuses, without justifiable reason, to provide a service to which he is obliged, shall be punished by a fine". According to the above, the driver may not charge more than the set payment for the service - commentators point out that this is rather the case when the price is regulated by law, maximum prices are set. It is also worth mentioning that the Constitutional Court, in its judgment of 26 June 2019, ref. K 16/17, declared Article 138, in the part containing the words 'or intentionally without good reason refuses to provide the service to which he is obliged', to be incompatible with Article 2 of the Constitution. The chance that a driver will be convicted for refusing to perform a ride due to a justifiable reason in the form of not having 'change' to give is considered to be very small.
** However, notwithstanding the above, the refusal to provide a service due to the lack of 'change' to be given may be considered to be incompatible with the principles of social co-existence and good morals. Furthermore, according to Article 59ea of the Payment Services Act, "A merchant may not make the conclusion of a service agreement or an agreement for the sale of goods with a consumer conditional on non-cash payment or refuse to accept payment from the consumer with monetary signs issued by the NBP."
** In our opinion, the worst model is one that forces the user to pay a higher amount if there is no amount exactly deducted and the driver has no 'change' to give. Such an action could theoretically qualify as:
(i) a practice that infringes the collective interests of consumers (Article 24(2) of the Act on Competition and Consumer Protection - a practice that infringes the collective interests of consumers is understood as conduct of an entrepreneur contrary to the law or good practice),
(ii) unfair market practice of a trader (Article 4(2) of the Act on Counteracting Unfair Market Practices - a market practice is unfair if it is contrary to good practice and materially distorts or is likely to distort the market behaviour of the average consumer before, during or after the conclusion of a product agreement).

Conclusions:

* *Will the information about the obligation to pay cash in advance in the app be sufficient*
** We believe that it is crucial that the payment rules are accurately described both in the terms and conditions and in the app. We agree that there is no established practice in this area, but it is in Bolt's interest that the consumer is accurately informed both through the content of the terms and conditions and in the app. This will limit the consumer's ability to plead ignorance or misrepresentation if he or she does not see before the ride that, for example, payment is made in advance.
** However, if it is, then how exactly should this be stated in the Terms and Conditions?
In the Terms and Conditions it could be added: "_In case of payment in cash, payment will be made in advance. In the event that change is required, the driver will be obliged to give the change. At the same time, we ask the user to carry a deducted sum of money corresponding to the fare, if possible. In spite of the driver's due diligence, it may happen that the driver does not have enough cash to give you the change. In this case, we ask the User to cancel the fare at no cost_."
* *Do we need to / can we indicate the consequences of not having the exact amount / change deducted in the terms and conditions, i.e. the possibility of the driver refusing the ride and having to order a new ride? In practice, this will mean cancellation of the ride either by the driver or by the user (but at no additional cost to the user). At this point, the user will not be able to change the payment method chosen when ordering the journey.*
** In our view, such consequences should be indicated in the terms and conditions, e.g. in the way we have proposed above. It is important that the refusal of a ride is not unjustified, while we understand that in practice there may be situations where the driver is unable to give change and cancellation is the only option. We believe that the key here is to clearly communicate to the consumer that such a situation may occur.

[@francisco.delavega|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U03GCGHN3KN] [@lea.lemonnier|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U035T3WCNQY] I think I know why that is happening.
Task can be closed by either charger or *cron* (automation).
Task opened by cron and closed by cron is basically a “noise” for you - it is not something we pay 3pl for and we don’t track them.Example of these tasks are:

* Coordinates of the scooter located and the edge of allowed zone jumps across the border of the zone and automatically the rebalance task is created. Once coordinates jump back to allowed zone task is closed automatically by cron.
* Another example. Scooter lost connection,  and search task is created but then scooter restores connection and search task closed automatically by cron.

Now. In the count of tasks opened at the beginning of the shift we include only tasks that are open at the beginning of the shift AND currently are either not resolved or resolved by charger. Because we don’t want this noise to mess the report (we know that msny of rebalance tasks are just a noise - they flicker, appearing and dissapearing)Imagine you run the report on 1st of May on that day a certain task is still open and we don’t know will it be closed by cron or not. Hey [~accountid:63da287e790148a18093a774] and [~accountid:62bbfa39ec4c0d377f9fc3b7], thanks a lot for all your help on this project so far 🙏 

There is one thing I would like to discuss with you before going back to business with specific schemes on how the legal relations should be established.

The following seems to be clear now:

* In EE the vehicles will be leased from the car provider by the local entity and subleased to both 1) drivers and 2) fleets. The majority of the fleets in EE are non-traditional fleets, meaning the transportation service provider is a driver (not fleet).
* In SE the vehicles will be leased from the car provider by the local entity and subleased to the fleets. The fleets in SE are traditional flees, meaning the transportation service provider is a fleet (not driver).

Now team has an issue with payment collection for the sublease of vehicles to either drivers or fleets. Hence, they would like to deduct sublease fees from the commission fee drivers and fleets are paying us for platform services. This is how it may be done:

* EE (sublease to drivers) - driver will give Bolt Ops a mandate to transfer part of driver’s earnings for the sublease to Bolt local entity. Therefore, the earnings will partially cover sublease and the rest will go to the driver as a payment for transportation services.
* EE (sublease to non-traditional fleets) - as the majority of the fleets in EE are not transportation service providers, I don’t really see a good way to transfer part of driver’s earnings to Bolt local entity, as the sublease agreement is concluded between Bolt local entity and the fleet whereas the platform services agreement is concluded between Bolt Ops and the driver. Hence, payment collection cannot happen with the set-off of driver earnings.
* SE (sublease to traditional fleets) - as in SE the fleets are transportation service providers, a similar deduction from commission as described for EE (sublease to drivers) should be legally possible.

I didn’t see any comments on this from [~accountid:63da287e790148a18093a774] but saw the comments on this from [~accountid:62bbfa39ec4c0d377f9fc3b7]. I also believe that in the ideal world there should be no deduction from commission to avoid reclassification risk to the maximum. However, considering the pain that the payment collection under sublease agreements might bring, I want to explore the deduction option with you. *How much do you see reclassification risk being increased in your markets if the payment under sublease agreement will be deducted from driver’s / fleet’s commission?*

* We would still be able to claim that:
** the vehicles are leased to the drivers / fleets at a market value (not for free),
** we still assume that driver / fleet has his own or leased vehicle while providing transportation services on our platform - the rental service we provide is an additional service to the platform service, the drivers are not anyhow forced to use it,
** the only point where two services intertwine is the payment collection process - as both services (platform and car sublease) are provided by Bolt, it makes sense for us to simplify the payment collection process.

What do you think of the above? Will it help with defending us from reclass claims or you see an obvious red flag for your markets if we collect payments this way and it is not worth exploring going forward? We may as well schedule a call if this is more convenient for both of you. Thanks a lot in advance!

Updated the existing Identity Type attribute mapping. The new mapping expression changes the value from CONTINGENT → EMPLOYEE given that the following attributes match the user’s Okta profile. 

* workerSubType: “B2B Contractors”

* employeeCountry: “Poland”

* the total consideration paid or credited each quarter of the given calendar year and the number of activities in respect of which the consideration was paid, and

x.country_code,
APPROX_DISTINCT(x.driver_id,0.0041) AS count_drivers,

ROUND(CAST(AVG(CASE WHEN x.ratio > 0.05 THEN x.client_did_not_pay_count END) AS double),2) AS avg_client_did_not_pay_count,
ROUND(CAST(APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN x.ratio > 0.05 THEN x.driver_id END,0.0041)*1.00/APPROX_DISTINCT(x.driver_id,0.0041) AS double),2) AS ratio_flagged
--ROUND(CAST(AVG(x.client_did_not_pay_count) AS double),2) AS avg_client_did_not_pay_count,
--ROUND(CAST(AVG(x.ratio) AS double),2) AS avg_ratio
FROM (
SELECT 
json_extract_scalar(a.input, '$.additional.order.driver_id') AS driver_id,
json_extract_scalar(a.input, '$.data.order_handle.city_id') AS city_id,
b.country_code,
json_extract_scalar(a.input, '$.additional.driver_historic_order_statistics.cash_count') AS cash_count,
CAST(json_extract_scalar(a.input, '$.additional.driver_historic_order_statistics.client_did_not_pay_count') AS bigint) AS client_did_not_pay_count,
CASE WHEN CAST(json_extract_scalar(a.input, '$.additional.driver_historic_order_statistics.cash_count') AS bigint) > 0 THEN CAST(json_extract_scalar(a.input, '$.additional.driver_historic_order_statistics.client_did_not_pay_count') AS bigint)*1.00/CAST(json_extract_scalar(a.input, '$.additional.driver_historic_order_statistics.cash_count') AS bigint) END AS ratio
FROM archive_analytical.rides_cs_issue a
LEFT JOIN ng_public.admin_system_city b ON CAST(json_extract_scalar(a.input, '$.data.order_handle.city_id') AS bigint) = b.id
WHERE a.created_hour >= date '2023-05-01'
AND CAST(json_extract_scalar(a.input, '$.additional.driver_historic_order_statistics.cash_count') AS bigint) > 100
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5
) AS x
GROUP BY 1 {noformat}

Please see an overview of all five proposals that we have received from different potential partners.[https://docs.google.com/document/d/1_xQrd74Cq8h99cABdz7ye7Bb1_ej-GVqkfy2ZM2UZUA/edit|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1_xQrd74Cq8h99cABdz7ye7Bb1_ej-GVqkfy2ZM2UZUA/edit|smart-link] The selection was based on partners’ ability to 1) deliver in short timelines; 2) credibility and image of the partner in transport/sustainability domain; 4) previous experience working on shared mobility and modelling economic and env benefits of shared mobility; 5) experience both in Africa and Europe. By aforementioned parameters OW scored the highest as compared to other proposals. Thus, after internal discussion, and consultation with all relevant internal stakeholders, it was decided to conduct this project with Oliver Wyman.

Just to elaborate on this in Malta they have the:

Malta Insurance Association (MIA) - [https://maltainsurance.org/|https://maltainsurance.org/|smart-link]

and 

Motor Insurance Bureau (MIB) - [https://maltainsurance.org/service/mib/|https://maltainsurance.org/service/mib/|smart-link]

The purpose of the MIB is to pay third parties should they suffer a loss from an uninsured vehicle/driver. 

Therefore, essentially when we have a user breach our T&Cs and the insurers' conditions i.e. _They are underage. They are Drunk, They are riding tandem etc, etc._ then they are uninsured. 

In the past, I have been told that if a third party tried to claim from our insurer in Malta (Gasan Mamo) and it is declined because of a breach of the T&Cs, the claimant then approaches us directly, and we pay them. 

However, since Malta has an uninsured driver scheme with the MIB. In theory, we could point the claimant to this. 

We could say the user breached the insurance conditions and is therefore not insured. As a result, you need to claim from the MIB and provide links etc.

I have insurance knowledge and background, but unfortunately, I have no local legal knowledge in Malta. Therefore, my concern was since we allowed the user to break the conditions i.e. _we did not validate they are underage or there were drunk etc_. could local laws still hold us/bolt responsible and therefore prevent the claimant from using the MIB?



The last point on this is we could lean on our insurer Gasan to pay these claims as the MIA very clearly says:

*Ineffective Policies – Breach of a Policy Condition by the Insured*

_“If there is an insurance policy in force which is however ineffective due to a breach of a policy condition, the insurer who issued this policy must still handle the relative third party claims._

_An insurer will handle such claims not out of a duty arising from the policy, but because he has undertaken with the MIB to act as if he were the insurer – to act as ‘insurer concerned’._

_This means that in this manner, a victim of an accident will not be deprived of third-party liability cover, notwithstanding the presence of certain conditions which would otherwise invalidate the relative policy. However, the insurer will be able to recover any payments which he has effected to the victim from the policyholder.”_

*BUT -* if we do lean on Gasan to pay these claims then they have the right to recover their losses from us since we are the policyholder. 

Therefore, claims which are solely are users' fault might be an issue; but where this could work is whereby there is another uninsured motorist involved. For example when our user has been hit.

Hey [~accountid:6151cf6878e5e40070fb74c2], please see below the analysis for Ukraine. Please let me know if you have any questions.

----

# *Is the market subject to laws where an employment relationship can be deemed or implied? Yes/no*

No, but the caselaw on deemed or implied employment relationship exists.
We would like to highlight that there are currently no binding legislative provisions on deemed or implied employment relationship.
However, in practice, any contractor arrangements between both Ukrainian resident, non- resident entities and their respective counterparties (individuals registered as private entrepreneurs or simply individuals) may potentially be subject to deemed or implied employment rules which are defined and assessed by the Ukrainian tax authorities, the State Labor Service of Ukraine and the courts (see sec. 4 for more details).

# *Is there any evidence that platforms are under scrutiny under the legal system (litigation etc)?*

No, there is no evidence that platforms are being or have been scrutinized under the legal system in Ukraine. There is also no evidence that the state authorities have applied the concept of deemed or implied employment relationship to the platform operators in Ukraine so far.
It is also worth noting that the concept of deemed or implied employment relationship has been discussed widely by the tax and other state authorities in Ukraine in relation to IT companies and their contractors – IT specialists. However, there the caselaw showing that any of the state authorities have ever targeted the IT business specifically for deemed or implied employment relationship is very limited in numbers so far.

# *Is the relevant test subject to express presumption criteria? Yes/no*

No, but some criteria exist in caselaw.
Although neither tax nor labour legislations of Ukraine provide for exhaustive list of criteria which may be applied as a reason for re-qualification of contractor arrangements into employment relations – alternative criteria is yet implied by the caselaw (see sec. 4 for more details).
Nevertheless, the Draft Law No. 5054-1 dated 25.02.2021 (the "Draft Law") proposes to incorporate an exhaustive list of the criteria based on the caselaw, as described above, to the Labor Code of Ukraine. Namely, the Draft Law implies introduction of the definition of an "employment agreement" and the test defining the existence of employment relations consisting of the following criteria: 
▪  work is performed on behalf of and under the control of the person in whose interests the work is performed;
▪ the work is of a permanent nature, with no references to the amount of tasks that need to be performed in a specified period of time;
▪  work is performed at the designated workplace;
▪  the facilitation of work (i.e. provision of equipment, tools, materials) is organized by the
person in whose interests the work is performed;
▪  the remuneration in cash and/or in kind is paid on a regular basis;
▪  the working hours are defined by the person in whose interests the work is performed;
▪  travel and other financial expenses related to the performance of the work are reimbursed by the person in whose interests the work is performed.
The Draft Law proposes to classify the activities that meet at least 6 requirements mentioned above as employment relationship.
The Draft Law is currently being under the review of the parliamentary committee. We recommend to follow the news and updates on this topic.

# *Are reclassification sensitive activities expressly considered by a court or any law to imply an employment relationship?*

The Ukrainian courts (and tax authorities as well) generally tend to focus in their assessments on how the contractor arrangements between both Ukrainian resident, non-resident entities and their respective counterparties (e.g. Ukrainian individuals registered as private entrepreneurs or simply individuals) are contractually structured.
Based on our analysis of the relevant caselaw, we have summarised below the key criteria which are frequently applied by the Ukrainian tax authorities and courts to define reasons for reclassification of contractor arrangements into employment relations:
▪ The work of the contractor is not independent and takes place within the framework of a certain enterprise, institution, organization (legal entity);
▪  Service recipient provides the Ukrainian contractor with working stations and any other required assets and infrastructure (e.g., equipment, software, etc. (including on a free-of-charge basis);
▪  The Ukrainian contractor is required to or _de facto_ complies with internal policies and regulations of a service recipient (e.g., working hours, etc.);
▪  Remuneration for the provided services is paid regularly and periodically (i.e. approximately at the same time for the same period) in mostly the same installments;
▪  There are specific requirements (e.g.,education, qualification, professional skills and/or state of health, etc.) to the Ukrainian contractor;
▪  Service recipient reimburses expenses of the Ukrainian contractor incurred in connection with the provision of services;
▪  Service recipient provides fringe benefits (e.g., meals, education allowance, wellness and wellbeing allowances, etc.) and/ or social security guarantees (e.g., paid annual leave, sick leave, etc.) to the Ukrainian contractor;
▪  The Ukrainian contractor receives most of its income from the same source.

# *Can claims be made in respect of past periods (i.e. for previously withheld earnings?)*

Yes, the tax authorities and other state authorities are eligible to make a claim against Bolt during the 3-year period starting from the date employment relations deemed to be concluded in relation to its respective tax obligations, other than the unified social contribution.
Please note that there is no statute of limitations for accrual of the unified social contribution, and thus, tax authorities may file a claim in relation to the unified social contribution for any past periods.
It is important to highlight that the standard 3-year statute of limitations period in 2020 has been postponed indefinitely until the end of COVID-19 quarantine measures in Ukraine and additionally, until the end of the martial law in Ukraine.

# *Who is able to take action against Bolt? Drivers / group action / regulators*

Individual drivers, groups of individuals/legal entities, state and local authorities, as well as regulators are eligible to make a claim against Bolt regarding reclassification of contractual relationship into employment relationship in Ukraine.
Bolt (as a non-resident legal entity) will be subject to the jurisdiction of Ukrainian courts on the basis that the services were performed by drivers on the territory of Ukraine.

# *Is there any evidence the authorities have considered drivers eligible for employment benefits in the past (e.g. tax authorities, pension authorities etc)?*

No, we are not aware of any cases of the state authorities having considered drivers eligible for employment benefits in the past.
Pursuant to a limited caselaw on this topic in Ukraine, the courts had to define whether the employment relations have existed at all in a few minor cases where the drivers claimed to be the employees of the platform operators. All the cases considered the level of responsibility of the drivers for the damaged property, while the court ruled in each case that the drivers were not the employees.

# *What is the level of access to justice in a market (e.g. high state duties, requirement to have a representative etc)?*

The level of access to justice in Ukraine can be described as "high" meaning that the courts and justice are accessible to most individuals and legal entities considering the following indicators:
▪  Factual accessibility of the courts during the martial law: the courts are currently fully functional;
▪  State duties and fees: the "court levy" is charged upon filing claims, complaints, and for the issuance of certain documents by the court. The amount of the court levy depends on the amount of the minimum living wage as of January 1 of the year in which the court levy should be payable (UAH 2,684 in 2023 (approximately EUR 78,98)). The amount of court levy may vary significantly depending on the type of the claim (i.e. whether criminal, civil, administrative or other proceeding) and the division of the court (i.e. district court, court of appeal or the Supreme Court).
▪  Representation requirement: currently only an attorney has a right to represent another person in a trial (the so-called "attorney monopoly”) in most of the cases (excluding minor cases of “simple complexity". Otherwise, an individual or a head (director) of a legal entity may represent themselves before the court without a need to appoint an attorney.

# *Can claims be made to reclassify all drivers of the platform in a market at once?*

Yes. As a matter of standard practice, the Ukrainian tax authorities are likely to treat all the drivers of the platform as having employment relations provided the Ukrainian tax authorities will be successful in challenging the status of even one single driver. This means that in the event if the tax authorities reclassify current employment relationship between Bolt and drivers, tax issues may potentially arise, in particular, the Ukrainian tax authorities may assess payroll taxes to Bolt. 
The employment benefits in Ukraine may be claimed only by separate individual or group claims of the drivers. However, there is no practical mechanism that enables group claims in Ukraine, and moreover, such cases of claiming employment benefits from a non-resident legal entity are quite extraordinary and very limited in numbers as for now.

General process for a schema would be:

# Copy slow log from MySQL master, which has long_query_time=0 (all our MySQL servers are set with that) to local computer
# Prepare and filter the slow query log with specific schema:
{noformat}pt-query-digest target-d1-slow.log.old --filter 'print Dumper $event' --no-report --sample 1

pt-query-digest --sample 25 --no-report --output slowlog pt-query-digest --filter '($event->{db} // "") eq "taxify_campaign_tests"' target-d1-slow.log.old > samples.log{noformat}
# Obtain a MySQL replica and a TiDB server with same data + replication stopped at same point in time
## This is the hardest part of the process since it is a lot of work, needs extra machines, storage and times time for larger datasets
## One possible option is to replicate from a MySQL replica to TiDB prelive using DM to replicate schema to test. Then stop replication on MySQL replica (a bit intrusive since all replicas have a specific purpose). This means no writes would happen to test schema, on both MySQL and TiDB hosts, allow pt-upgrade to run.
## Second option would be to setup separate MySQL dedicated replica and new TiDB testing cluster. This would imply much higher costs of infra structure. 
# Run pt-upgrade against both servers twice, once for warming up DB, second to get warmed up query results
{noformat}pt-upgrade h=mysql_hostname,P=3306,u=root,p=... h=tidb_hostname,P=4000,u=root,p=... --max-examples=1 samples.log 1> pt-upgrade-results.out 2>pt-upgrade-results.err{noformat}
# Review differences [https://docs.percona.com/percona-toolkit/pt-upgrade.html#report|https://docs.percona.com/percona-toolkit/pt-upgrade.html#report|smart-link]

# *Subjective scope of the proposed agreement*

From a tax perspective, we ([~accountid:61b9ad7c2900b00071da0b68] and me) see no problem to include within the scope of the agreement the affiliates of each party (Bolt Group affiliates and Schenker Group affiliates) that may get involved in the material supply of the services envisaged by the agreement. However, please see some further comments below. 

*2. Tax implications arising from the proposed billing setup.*

In line with the input by [~accountid:61cc1c959ee70a00680edd89] , it seems that under the proposed billing structure all purchase orders would be concluded between Bolt Operations OÜ and Schenker AS, so all invoices and payments of all the services supplied under the Agreement would happen between these two entities.

From a tax standpoint, such billing flow would trigger the following implications:

* Allocation of costs to the companies actually benefiting from the services provided by Schenker: There might be cases where the costs initially borne (and paid) by Bolt Ops would have to be passed through to the relevant Bolt local companies that ultimately benefit from the service provided by Schenker. Such a setup may entail a significant increase in the workload from an accounting perspective and billing perspective. What do you think [~accountid:60b2030e25a51300698c52c6] and [~accountid:6131df23b1894f00718e9faa] ?
* It may trigger VAT and Customs implications and an increase in the VAT compliance workload, as a consequence of the aforementioned recharge of costs amongst bolt group entities.
* It may trigger transfer pricing implications (TBC with the TP team).

 *3. Master Agreement and direct billing setup.*

In order to mitigate the above-mentioned adverse consequences, it may be preferable to conclude a *Master Services Agreement* (“MSA”) between Bolt Ops OÜ and AS Schenker governing the general framework of the services to be supplied by AS Schenker and its affiliates to Bolt Ops OÜ and to the Bolt Group affiliates. Such a MSAwould allow the entities belonging to both multinational groups (i.e. those involved in the supply of services) to liaise with each other, thus creating a *direct billing flow amongst them*. The affiliates involved in the supply of the services would not need to enter into separate agreements but only issue purchase orders within the framework of the MSA.

Under such a scenario, the tax implications may be outlined as follows:

* There would be no need to pass through any costs from Bolt Ops OÜ to any of the Bolt Group affiliates as the invoice would be issued to and the cost booked in the correct Bolt entity from the outset.
* The MSA would be seamless from a VAT perspective and, thus,  not increase the VAT compliance workload.
* No TP implications would arise because there would be no inter-company transactions.

+EXAMPLES:+

# +Services provided by Schenker AS to Bolt Ops OÜ in relation to cross-border verticals (micro-mobility and food delivery).+

* The service cost would be directly borne (and allocated) to the company performing as the principal supplier of micro-mobility and food delivery services (i.e. Bolt Ops OÜ)
* In accordance with the EU VAT Directive, intra-community B2B services of transportation of goods are deemed to take place where the recipient of the service is established. Therefore, services provided by AS Schenker to Bolt Ops would be subject to EE VAT, regardless of the place where the transportation starts and finishes (TBC with VAT team)

* No TP implications would arise because there are no inter-company transactions.

+2. Services provided in relation to localized verticals (micro-mobility in some countries and Bolt Market).+

* The transportation service would be supplied by Schenker local company to Bolt Group local company, so the cost would be directly borne (and allocated) to the company performing as the principal supplier of micro-mobility and market services. No need to pass through any cost.
* The Bolt Group local company receiving the service would have to settle the VAT accrued as a consequence of the transportation service. In principle, no adverse VAT consequences may be expected.
* No TP implications would arise because there are no inter-company transactions.

 We will be looking forward to hearing from you about the approach above, and will be happy to help in the implementation of such an approach if needed.

Thank you, and have a good day.

h2. Reusable solution for reimporting images for a menu - edit 1

* Made a minor adjustment to [~accountid:623ace2d7910a200718aec2d] 's script by moving the row_count() call right after menu_item_image_job rows insertions.

{code:sql}-- (1) If you're starting from providers, first get the list of menus & vendors
select
    distinct b.vendor_id, a.menu_id
from
    provider_active_menu a
inner join
    menu_version b on a.menu_id = b.menu_id
where
    a.provider_id in (46405, 48838, 53476, 46818, 46822, 46823, 53477, 53478, 56696, 46824, 47150, 53474, 53475, 64953);

-- (2) Configure the parameters below
select @reason := 'https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/DPM-816';
select @vendor_id := 32412;
select @menu_id := 1765068173;

-- (3) For each menu & vendor pair do:

-- (3.1) Start a new transaction
begin;

-- (3.2) Set to 'pending' rows from menu_item_image
with menu_item_image_ids as
    (
    select 
        distinct b.id
    from
        menu_item a
    inner join
        menu_item_image b on b.image_url_crc = CRC32(JSON_UNQUOTE(JSON_EXTRACT(params, "$.images[0].source_info.url")))
    where
        a.menu_id = @menu_id
        and b.vendor_id = @vendor_id
        and a.params like '%source_info%'
    )
update
    menu_item_image a
inner join
    menu_item_image_ids b on a.id = b.id
set
    a.state = 'pending',
    a.tries_no = 0,
    a.scheduled_timestamp = NOW(),
    a.reason = @reason
where
    a.id > 0 -- so that MySQL Workbench allows executing this query
;

-- (3.3) Insert new jobs in menu_item_image_job
insert into menu_item_image_job(
    menu_item_id,
    menu_item_image_id,
    menu_id,
    priority,
    state,
    scheduled_timestamp,
    reason
)
select 
    a.id, -- menu_item_id
    b.id, -- menu_item_image_id
    a.menu_id, -- menu_id
    3, -- priority
    'pending', -- state
    NOW(), -- scheduled_timestamp
    @reason -- reason
from
    menu_item a
inner join

    and a.params like '%source_info%'
;

select max(id) into @maxid from menu_item_image_job;

{noformat}with blocking_duration as (
select 
fc.city_id as city_id,
event_timestamp_date as date,
ic.external_id as driver_id,
count(*) as blocking_event_count,
sum(etl.blocked_duration) as blocked_duration_min,
sum(etl.blocked_duration/60) as blocked_duration_h
from ng_public.etl_billing_cashblock_rides etl
left join ng_public.invoicing_client ic on ic.id = etl.client_id and ic.type = 'Driver'
left join ng_public.fleet_company fc on fc.id = ic.company_id 
where fc.country = 'gh'
and etl.is_unblocked = 1
and etl.event_timestamp_date >= DATE('2023-05-01')
group by 1,2,3
),
last_ride as (
select 
etl.city_id as city_id,
etl.driver_id as driver_id,
max(period_local_date) as last_ride_date
from ng_public.etl_driver_hourly_activity etl
left join ng_public.admin_system_city asc2 on asc2.id = etl.city_id 
where etl.finished_orders > 0
and asc2.country_code = 'gh'
and etl.period_local_date >= DATE('2023-04-01')
group by 1,2
)
select 
lr.city_id,
lr.driver_id,
lr.last_ride_date,
DATE(bd.date) as blocking_event_date,
bd.blocking_event_count,
bd.blocked_duration_min,
bd.blocked_duration_h
from last_ride lr 
left join blocking_duration bd on bd.city_id = lr.city_id and bd.driver_id = lr.driver_id
where lr.last_ride_date >= DATE(current_date - interval '30' day){noformat}

Hi [~accountid:604aad6558aa8d00722fb03f], thanks for raising this. We unfortunately already had [similar incidents|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/4339598228/2023-03-03+DE+Data+lake+backfill+exhausted+resources+of+TiDB+beta+cluster] in the past, but wasn’t aware yet of this one.

The backfill should of course not affect backend performance. It is not always easy though to find the right balance between running “fast enough” (backfills can take weeks or even months if batches are too small) and avoiding impact on the source database. We still have some improvements to do there.

You should not need to test the queries. We have already added some heuristic to flag potentially problematic backfills automatically in the PR’s, which also did detect this table:

!Screenshot 2023-05-22 at 10.49.17.png|width=736,height=228!

And that heuristic was the reason why the predicate was added to the query, which already should have reduced the impact on the backend database quite a bit. Since that apparently still wasn’t enough, we indeed also should have adjusted the batch size via the {{scanChunkSizeInRows}} parameter.

This batch size parameter is undocumented because it’s a bit tricky to use, and we hope to automate the process of finding “correct” batch size to prevent such incidents in the future. The current implementation simply uses the configured (or default) batch size however, regardless of how long queries take.

We’ll keep improving both the heuristics to detect problematic backfills, and the adjustments to make them work without (or at least less) issues, and will hopefully have less such incidents in the future. Until then, please always raise the issue somewhere (as a ticket here, or if more urgent on Slack via {{#dev-data-platform-support}}) when you see it, so that we know which cases we still need to fix.

There are no specific laws/rules for such situations, however, the consumer protection law says: The offering and sale, and marketing in any other manner, of goods and services to consumers *shall follow good trade practice and be honest with regard to consumers*. The offering of goods or services shall be planned and carried out in a manner whereby the commercial *purpose of the offer is clear* to consumers.

Based on that, I would say that we should communicate this. I don’t think we specifically need to state that “3 bananas are allowed” but leave a disclaimer that the quantity of goods per order might be limited at Bolt’s own discretion.

Thank you [~accountid:5eda5d0647291b0b8608735a] for the below explanations:

Bolt Operations should conclude *a free-rent agreement (Romanian “contract comodat”)* with the municipality regarding the free use of the scooters by the municipality. The agreement should mention that the ownership of the scooters remains with Bolt Operations, whereas Bolt Operations supports the maintenance expenses.

Article 271 par. (4) letter a) of the Romanian Fiscal Code includes amongst the deliveries of services the use of goods used in the economic activity, which are made available, for free use, to other people, for purposes other than carrying out his economic activity, if the VAT for the respective goods has been fully or partially deducted.

Thus, Bolt Operations (Romanian VAT code) should issue a self-invoice to itself regarding the input VAT related to the maintenance of the scooters and include as taxable base in the self-invoice all expenses (including maintenance) incurred with the scooters given for free to the municipality.

To summarise what we discussed on the call on 8th May: 

Potential liability for Bolt may arise under section 21 of the Traffic Transport Law if, by facilitating the provision of taxi services through its platform, *Bolt is found by a court to have* +*caused, allowed or tolerated*+ *the use of a vehicle by a taxi driver or a non-taxi driver in contravention of the relevant law (e.g. by introducing dynamic pricing)*.

We are talking here about +criminal liability+ and being subject to imprisonment for a period not exceeding six months and/or to a fine not exceeding EUR 768. In addition, if a person is found guilty of the above offence by a court, and consequently refuses to comply or does not comply with such court order, he/she/it may be found guilty of a criminal offence and may be subject to imprisonment for a period not exceeding one year and/or to a fine not exceeding EUR 1,710.

It is unfortunately, as we discussed on the call, very difficult to give any probability to this risk arising, but as mentioned above, the criminal sanction would follow a court conviction. There is no precedent for a platform/mediator being found liable under section 21 at this point so this remains +untested+ in the Cypriot courts - but does not mean that we could not be the first one. 

External counsel also considered the point about us being a cross-border provider (Bolt Ops from EE) under Directive 2000/31/EC (the E-Commerce Directive) which was implemented in Cyprus by Law 156(I)/2004 (the “*Law*”). However their summary is that the Law does not afford any protection to information service societies established in other Member States and operating in Cyprus +in relation to criminal penalties+ imposed following a criminal investigation or criminal proceedings, which would include the penalty envisioned in relation to breach of section 21 of the Regulation of Traffic Transport of 1982 (L.9/1982) (as amended). So unfortunately this does not alleviate us of the risk. 

Please let me know if you should have any further queries. 

Best, 

Liisa

Currently RVP sets a threshold so that false positive rate is 10% (meaning out of order tries that are accepted, it predicts rejection in 10% cases). This is a flawed approach and leads to model being too aggressive in cities with low rejection rate and not aggressive enough in cities with high rejection rate. Aggressiveness tuning (untested so far) allowed to change 10% to be between 1% and 22.5%, but default case is not optimal.

I suggest a new solution in which parameter alpha in (0,1) is set (default 0.5) and model aims to satisfy false_positive_count = alpha * false_negative_count.

* in the least aggressive case the model has zero false positives - in practice it means it never predicts a rejection
* in default case threshold is set so that one false positive is worth 2 true positives
* in most aggressive case it holds that predicted_rejection_rate = true_rejection_rate. So it is not possible to overdo aggressiveness.

That approach proves to have more reasonable predicted_rejection_rates in default case. Backtest results to follow. The only downside of the approach is an edge case of a model with auc_roc <= 0.5. In such case we should probably predict no rejections - but that should not happen, definitely not in a major city.

* Minimal balance to unblock cash rides = *-10 000 tzs* (50% of the blocking limit)
* Minimal balance left on driver balance = 0 tzs (unrelated to cash-blocking)

+*DLA assessment:*+ 

* _Does the data scraping activity described above (route fare + ETA data collection, walled-off behind terms of service and account login) could attract criminal liability under the applicable Portuguese law?_ 

The short answer is “yes”, as we will explain. We think it is worth making two introductory remarks.

First, {color:#bf2600}the legal rules regarding both unfair competition and legal protection of databases do not provide for any criminal liability. The sanctions in both these cases are administrative offences, which may attract fines, but are not criminal offences.{color}

Second, it is relevant whether the described activity will involve the processing of personal data. The data at stake – prices and estimated duration of trips – does not contain personal data. However, it is not clear from the description if the data scraping will involve processing of personal data in accordance with the GDPR. The legal definitions of “processing” and “personal data” under the GDPR are very broad, and any access to personal data will be subject to the GDPR. We will consider this in our explanation below.

If the activity involves processing of personal data, there are two crimes which could apply:

# Article 193 of the Criminal Code – Illegal probe using information systems _(“Devassa por meio da informática”_) – which is described as creating, maintaining or using files containing individually identifiable data relating to private life (user trips) without consent or legal grounds. This crime is punishable with a maximum prison sentence of 2 years. Please note this specific crime cannot be charged to legal persons, so in practical terms is not relevant for Bolt.
# Article 47 of Law 58/2019, of 8 August (legislation implementing the GDPR in Portugal) – Undue Access (_“Acesso indevido”_) – which is described as access in any way to personal data, without due authorization or justification. This crime is punishable with a maximum prison sentence of 1 year. This amount is raised to 2 years if circumvention of technical measures occurs, which should be considered here as data is protected by account login. Please note this specific crime can be charged to legal persons.

Regardless of whether the activity involves processing of personal data, there is one crime which could apply:

# Article 6 of the Cybercrime Law – Illegitimate Access (_“Acesso ilegítimo”_) – which is described as access to a computer system without legal permission or without being authorized to do so by the owner. This crime is punishable with a maximum prison sentence of 1 year. This amount is raised to 5 years if circumvention of technical measures occurs, which should be considered here as data is protected by account login. Please note this specific crime can be charged to legal persons.

Fines may be applied in lieu of a prison sentence. Fines are calculated on the number of days, and a 1 year prison sentence corresponds to 120 days. The value of a day is calculated based on the economic situation of the accused, with a maximum of EUR 500.00.

In this sense, as Illegitimate Access is punishable with a maximum prison sentence of 5 years, this corresponds to 600 days, so the maximum applicable fine for this crime is EUR 300,000.00.

* _Is terms of service prohibition a precondition?_

No, the criminal offences may occur if the facts match the description of the relevant crimes. The terms of service are contractual terms which do not bind third parties (such as Bolt or the service provider doing the data scraping).

It is not relevant if the terms of service prohibit data scraping.

* _What kind of test is applied?_

The test corresponds to matching (or not) the facts with the description of the criminal offence. The premise is that the envisaged data scraping activities will be carried out without the authorisation from the competitors. In this sense the relevant tests are:

# For Undue Access (Article 47 of Law 58/2019, of 8 August), whether +there is access to personal data+. If no personal data is involved, there is no risk of liability.
# For Illegitimate Access (Article 6 of the Cybercrime Law), whether +there is access to the computer systems of a competitor+. If data is scraped from publicly accessible databases, there is no risk of liability.

* _Does it equally apply to manual data extraction and automated script/crawler based data extraction?_

Yes, the crimes apply equally to both methods. Using automated scripts/ crawlers may make it easier to avoid processing personal data, but this is the only difference.

* _What is the likelihood of criminal liability to arise (0%-100%)?_

{color:#bf2600}Likelihood will depend on whether this activity is detected, and specifically with regard to Undue Access, on whether personal data in processed.{color}

{color:#bf2600}Actual risk depends on whether affected competitors decide to file a criminal complaint. This is not a very relevant risk because from a strategic perspective a criminal complaint is not a very efficient means to react. Companies in Portugal are more likely to resort to the civil courts, to seek an injunction to stop this activity and / or ask for damages. Criminal investigations are impossible to control and the outcome is uncertain.{color}

If the activity is detected, a criminal compliant is filed and an investigation reveals evidence of illegitimate access, I would say that the likelihood of criminal liability to arise is relatively high, between 60-70%.

{color:#bf2600}Actual risk in my opinion would be much lower, somewhere between 20-30%.{color}

* _Which individual working at Bolt would be exposed to criminal sanctions (both imprisonment and fines) - i.e. is it ‘only’ the company director(s) (administrador de direito) or could it also affect the company employees (performing the data scraping and/or aware of it), the de facto manager (administrador de facto), and/or the CEO?_

{color:#bf2600}Bolt as a legal person is liable for criminal activity in the two crimes described above. In our experience, when legal persons are involved, and a conviction occurs, the court only applies a fine.{color}

{color:#bf2600}We are not aware of any case where a prison sentence was applied to a legal person in the types of criminal offences we are discussing here{color}.

{color:#bf2600}In any case, exposure to prison sentences is limited to the members of the corporate bodies of the legal person. Company employees or managers would not be exposed to sanctions.{color}

{color:#bf2600}Individuals would not be exposed to fines, except is very rare situations, such as when the company is bankrupt and unable to pay the fines.{color}

Please note we are not addressing a scenario where employees are acting outside or against company instructions; in these cases, they could be directly criminally liable, and not as employees of Bolt.

{color:#6554c0}+*Summary of claim letter*+ {color}

Mr Syed Haider has issued a letter to Bolt (letter dated 13 May 2023), the contents of the letter states that he wants to bring a claim against Bolt and the Passenger for ‘Defamation of Character’. He has expressed that he wants Bolt to respond to the letter within 14 days (this means the deadline to respond is 27 May 2023) otherwise he will issue court proceedings for recovery of his losses for “serious harm” at £200 plus legal fees. 

{color:#6554c0}+*AB comments and research*+ {color}

*Relevant legislation*: Defamation Act 2013, Defamation Act 1996, Common Law, Human Rights Act 1998 and Media Industry Codes of practice.

*CPR rules:* The rules on Defamation are primarily contained in CPR 53, Practice Direction 53A and 53B. 

{color:#6554c0}*How to prove a claim for Defamation*{color}

There are two types of defamation and the claimant must decided which form of defamation to bring a claim in: 

# *Libel:* this is defamation in permeant form it includes printed matter (newspapers, magazines and books), but also recordings and transmissions, media broadcast, radio, film, social media and internet transmissions. 
# *Slander:* is a transient form of defamation, and s usually made by word of mouth for example: unrecorded speech. By nature as it is not reproduced it is seen as the less serious form in contrast to Libel. 

{color:#6554c0}*In order to bring a claim the claimant must establish:* {color}

# *Publication* (communication to a third party): it must have been communicated to a third party, it is not enough to show that the statement is only made to the claimant. This is because the claimants reputation if it has only been communicated to them. 
# *The language must be defamatory:* the words must lower the claimant in the estimation of right thinking members of society, this is an objective test. The words are given there natural and ordinary construction. 
# *Which identifies or refers to the claimant*: The claimant must prove that the statement identifies him. This is usually shown by reference to the claimants name/photograph/description/by implication/by title, this is an objective test. 
# *Which has caused or is likely to cause serious harm to reputation of the claimant:* under section 1 Defamation Act 2013 in order for a statement to be considered defamatory its publication must cause or be likely to cause serious harm to the reputation of the claimant. 
# If the claimant satisfies and proves the above (point 1-4) cause of action in defamation has been made out, the law then presumes the words are false and the burden of proof shifts to the defendant. The defendant must then show that the words are true or to raise an alternative defence. 

{color:#6554c0}*Defences to a Defamation Claim:*{color}

# *Truth:* under section 2 Defamation Act 2013, this applies when the defendant can show that the allegation conveyed by the statement is true. 
# *Honest opinion:* section 2 Defamation Act 2013, the following must be established to successfully raise this defence: statement of opinion, statement must indicate the basis of the opinion, opinion must be honestly held. Note: this defence can be defeated if the claimant can demonstrate that the opinion was not honestly held by the defendant (under section 3(5), this is a subjective test). 
# *Absolute privilege:* this defence is a matter of public policy even when the statements have caused harm and malice. These statements mainly relate to situations such as statements made in parliamentary proceedings,  judicial proceedings and statements made to the police.
# *Qualified privilege:* there are 4 types of qualified privilege (statutory qualified privilege-s.15 DA 1996, common law privilege, peer reviewed statements in scientific or academic journals, publication on the matter of public interest). 
# *Innocent dissemination:*section 1 Defamation Act 1996 provides a defence to a person involved in the commercial distribution of a publication which is not the person responsible for the publication (example: person is not the  author, editor, publisher) and did not knowingly cause or contribute to its publication and took all reasonable care in relation to the publication.
# *Operators of websites:* under Section 5 DA 2013: this defence will apply if the operator can show that they did not post it on their website. 
# *Offer to make amends:* this is an alternative to raising a defence, this is when the defendant puts in writing an offer to make amends.

*My first assessment:*
A person is identifiable if the information is not sufficient in itself to assign it to a person, but it is possible as soon as the information is combined with other information. If it is possible to identify the person with the help of  other available information and other mean. Thus, all objective factors, such as the cost of identification and the time required, shall be taken into account. *In particular, the technologies available at the time of processing as well as technological developments shall be taken into account.*

*Knowledge and the means of third parties:* The GDPR does not provide any clear indications as to whether a relative or absolute reference to a person is to be assumed _(if the establishment of the reference to a person depends on the respective controller, this is referred to as a relative reference to a person; if the view is taken that it is sufficient that any third party can establish the reference to a person, this is referred to as an absolute reference to a person)._ In order to determine whether an individual is identifiable, account must be taken of all the means likely, in all probability, to be used *by the controller or by any other person* to identify the natural person. According to recital 26, the means to be explicitly considered in assessing the question of identifiability are those *that may be used by "another person" "to identify the individual directly or indirectly."* An absolute consideration could be inferred here. However, the use of the means by the third party must be *"reasonably likely."* This speaks in favor of a relative understanding, since the third party must come into contact with the data in question, e.g., it must have been transmitted to him. At the very least, however, according to recital 26, the conclusion seems permissible that it is not sufficient that any person anywhere in the world could establish the personal connection.
The ECJ's case law on the personal reference of IP addresses also indicates a relative understanding. In German case law and literature, however, different opinions can be found. 

The ECJ has provided initial approaches to interpreting IP addresses, but the question has not been conclusively resolved. Whether IP addresses are personal data depends on the *identifiability of the natural person using the IP address.* IP addresses are personal data if it is possible to establish a personal link to the stored data by legally permissible means. This can be done by an Internet service provider, *but if there is no legally permissible means of identification for the person who knows the IP address, it is considered to be indirectly personal data* (in view of this view, dynamic IP addresses are to be classified as personal data in any case as long as Internet service providers store assignment data that permits such identification, for example data relating to the question of which IP address is assigned to which customer at what time).
--> In case of traceability by BOLT: indirectly personal data.

*Result:* The data must be aggregated/processed in such a way that an assignment to a person is not possible or only possible with great difficulty (manual comparison of a large amount of data). Here we could check with our scooters team if a removal of the first 50-100 meters and an aggregation/bundling of data in certain time intervals is possible.


*Sources:* 
_Klar/Kühling_ in _Kühling/Buchner,_ DS-GVO Art 4 Nr 1 Rz 25 mwN.
_Hödl_ in _Knyrim,_ DatKomm Art 4 DSGVO (Stand 1.12.2018, [rdb.at|http://rdb.at])
EuGH 19. 10. 2016, C-582/14, _Breyer._

{code:sql}properties AS(
      SELECT
        m.id AS modal_id
        , m.name AS modal_name
        , CASE WHEN m."type" = 'dynamic' THEN 'modal' ELSE m."type" END "type"
        , DATE(mpc."start") AS start_date
        , DATE(mpc."end") AS end_date
        , mpc.state AS modal_status
        , mpc.id AS modal_poll_campaign_id
        , mpc.provider_id as provider_id
        , CASE WHEN REGEXP_LIKE(LOWER(m.name), 'bm|market') THEN 'market' ELSE 'food' END AS vertical
        , CASE WHEN DATE(mpc."end") < CURRENT_DATE THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS has_ended
        , CASE WHEN REGEXP_LIKE(LOWER(m.name), 'experiment|exp') THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS is_experiment
      FROM ${modal_modal.SQL_TABLE_NAME} AS m
      LEFT JOIN ${modal_modal_poll_campaign.SQL_TABLE_NAME} AS mpc ON m.id = mpc.modal_id
      WHERE
        m."domain" = 'eater'
        AND m."type" IN ('dynamic','banner','grouped_banner')
      )

      -- Joining modal_action and modal_poll_entry to tie unique action to modal_id and user_id per day.
    , modal_action AS(
      SELECT
        a.modal_poll_entry_id
        , a.created
          , CASE WHEN a."action" =  'view' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS flag_view
        , CASE WHEN a."action" =  'click' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS flag_click
        , CASE WHEN a."action" =  'close' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS flag_close
        , pe.modal_poll_campaign_id
        , pe.modal_id
        , pe.user_id
        , pe.country
        , pe.city_id
        , pe."language"
        FROM ${modal_modal_poll_entry.SQL_TABLE_NAME} AS pe
      LEFT JOIN ${modal_modal_action.SQL_TABLE_NAME} AS a ON a.modal_poll_entry_id = pe.id
      LEFT JOIN (SELECT id AS modal_id, "domain" FROM ${modal_modal.SQL_TABLE_NAME} GROUP BY 1,2) AS m ON pe.modal_id = m.modal_id
      WHERE
        m.domain = 'eater'
        AND a."action"  IN ('view','click','close')
      )

      -- Summarizing total modal interaction on user level per modal per day.
    , interaction AS(
      SELECT
        modal_poll_campaign_id
        , modal_id
        , user_id
        , country
        , city_id
        , "language"
        , DATE(created) AS created_date
        , SUM(COALESCE(flag_view,0)) AS total_view
        , SUM(COALESCE(flag_click,0)) AS total_click
        , SUM(COALESCE(flag_close,0)) AS total_close
      FROM modal_action
      GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5,6,7
      )

      , conversion AS(
        SELECT
          modal_poll_campaign_id
          , modal_id
          , user_id
          , country
          , city_id
          , "language"
          , DATE(COALESCE(last_food_interaction, last_market_interaction)) AS created_date
          , COUNT(CASE WHEN rn_food = 1 THEN food_order_id END) AS total_food_conversion
          , COUNT(CASE WHEN rn_market = 1 THEN market_order_id END) AS total_market_conversion
        FROM(
          SELECT *
            , ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY last_food_interaction, user_id, modal_id) AS rn_food
            , ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY last_market_interaction, user_id, modal_id) AS rn_market
          FROM(
          SELECT
            ma.modal_poll_campaign_id
            , ma.modal_id
            , ma.user_id
            , ma.country
            , ma.city_id
            , ma."language"
            , provider_id 
            , CASE WHEN c.trait_id IS NULL AND c.created BETWEEN ma.created AND DATE_ADD('hour',24,ma.created) THEN c.order_id END AS food_order_id
            , CASE WHEN c.trait_id = 145 AND c.created BETWEEN ma.created AND DATE_ADD('hour',24,ma.created) THEN c.order_id END AS market_order_id
            -- The calculation below is to determine the first transaction when there are two or more consecutive transaction
            , MAX(ma.created) OVER (PARTITION BY CASE WHEN c.trait_id IS NULL AND c.created BETWEEN ma.created AND DATE_ADD('hour',24,ma.created) THEN c.order_id END, ma.user_id, ma.modal_id) AS last_food_interaction
            , MAX(ma.created) OVER (PARTITION BY CASE WHEN c.trait_id = 145 AND c.created BETWEEN ma.created AND DATE_ADD('hour',24,ma.created) THEN c.order_id END, ma.user_id, ma.modal_id) AS last_market_interaction
          FROM(SELECT modal_poll_campaign_id, modal_id, user_id, country, city_id, "language", created FROM modal_action WHERE flag_view = 1) AS ma
          LEFT JOIN(
            SELECT
              oo.created
              , oo.master_user_id
              , oo.id AS order_id
              , pt.trait_id
            FROM ng_delivery.delivery_order_order AS oo
            LEFT JOIN ng_delivery.delivery_provider_provider_trait AS pt
              ON oo.provider_id = pt.provider_id
              AND pt.trait_id = 145
            WHERE
              oo.state = 'delivered'
            ) AS c
          ON c.master_user_id = ma.user_id
          WHERE c.created BETWEEN ma.created AND DATE_ADD('hour',24, ma.created)
          ))
        WHERE rn_food= 1 OR rn_market = 1
        GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5,6,7
        )

      -- Combining total interaction and conversion data along with the properties on user_id level for each modal each day.
      -- To count uniqueness of metrics, perform count(distinct case when total_click > 0 then user_id end) and aggregate them on modal_id level.
      SELECT
        i.modal_poll_campaign_id
        , i.modal_id
        , i.user_id
        , i."language"
        , i.created_date
        , p.modal_name
        , p."type"
        , p.start_date
        , p.end_date
        , p.modal_status
        , p.vertical
        , p.has_ended
        , p.is_experiment
        , ci.name AS city_name
        , co.name AS country_name
        , i.total_view
        , i.total_click
        , i.total_close
        , provider_id
        , COALESCE(CASE WHEN vertical = 'market' THEN total_market_conversion ELSE total_food_conversion END,0) AS total_conversion
      FROM interaction AS i
      LEFT JOIN conversion AS c
        ON i.modal_poll_campaign_id = c.modal_poll_campaign_id
        AND i.modal_id = c.modal_id
        AND i.user_id = c.user_id
        AND i.country = c.country
        AND i.city_id = c.city_id
        AND i."language" = c."language"
        AND i.created_date = c.created_date
      LEFT JOIN properties AS p ON i.modal_id = p.modal_id AND i.modal_poll_campaign_id = p.modal_poll_campaign_id
      LEFT JOIN ng_public.admin_system_city AS ci ON i.city_id = ci.id
      LEFT JOIN ng_public.admin_system_country AS co ON i.country = co.code{code}

*offline_ride_pickup_cancellation*


{code:sql}WITH abusers AS (
SELECT 
k.driver AS driver_id,
k.city_id AS city_id,
COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN k.pattern1 = 1 THEN k.order_id END) AS destination_cancellations,
COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN k.driver_rejection = 1 THEN k.order_id END) AS count_driver_rejections,
COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN k.pattern1 = 1 THEN k.order_id END)*1.00 / COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN k.driver_rejection = 1 THEN k.order_id END) AS ratio_destination_cancellations_in_all_rejections  -- against valid rejections 
FROM (
SELECT DISTINCT 
o.id AS order_id, 
o.created AS order_created,  
otl.city_id AS city_id,
o.country AS country,
ot.driver_id AS driver,
CASE WHEN o.state = 'no_driver_provided' AND ot.state = 'driver_rejected' AND otl.to_state = 'driver_rejected' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS driver_rejection,
CASE WHEN o.state = 'no_driver_provided' AND ot.state = 'driver_rejected' AND otl.from_state = 'driver_accepted' AND otl.to_state = 'driver_rejected' AND (DATEDIFF(minute, o.created, otl.created) >= ot.time_to_client_estimate) AND ROUND((111.111 *
    DEGREES(ACOS(LEAST(1.0, COS(RADIANS(o.lat))
         * COS(RADIANS(otl.lat))
         * COS(RADIANS(o.lng - otl.lng))
         + SIN(RADIANS(o.lat))
         * SIN(RADIANS(otl.lat))))))*1000) < 200 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS pattern1
FROM 
ng_public_spark.company_order AS o
JOIN ng_public_spark.company_order_try as ot ON ot.city_id = o.city_id AND o.id=ot.order_id 
JOIN ng_public_spark.company_order_try_state_log as otl ON otl.city_id = ot.city_id AND otl.order_try_id = ot.id
WHERE 
o.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
AND ot.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
AND otl.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE) 
AND o.state = 'no_driver_provided' AND ot.state = 'driver_rejected' AND otl.to_state = 'driver_rejected'
) AS k 
GROUP BY 1,2 
HAVING 
COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN k.pattern1 = 1 THEN k.order_id END) > 10 
AND 
COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN k.pattern1 = 1 THEN k.order_id END)*1.00 / COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN k.driver_rejection = 1 THEN k.order_id END) >= 0.6
) 
SELECT 
o.city_id || ':' || o.id AS KEY,
1 as offline_ride_pickup_cancellation
FROM 
ng_public_spark.company_order AS o
JOIN ng_public_spark.company_order_try as ot ON ot.city_id = o.city_id AND o.id=ot.order_id 
JOIN abusers AS a ON a.driver_id = ot.driver_id 
JOIN ng_public_spark.company_order_try_state_log as otl ON otl.city_id = ot.city_id AND otl.order_try_id = ot.id
WHERE 
o.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
AND ot.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
AND otl.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
AND o.state = 'no_driver_provided' AND ot.state = 'driver_rejected' AND otl.from_state = 'driver_accepted' AND otl.to_state = 'driver_rejected' AND (DATEDIFF(minute, o.created, otl.created) >= ot.time_to_client_estimate) AND ROUND((111.111 *
    DEGREES(ACOS(LEAST(1.0, COS(RADIANS(o.lat))
         * COS(RADIANS(otl.lat))
         * COS(RADIANS(o.lng - otl.lng))
         + SIN(RADIANS(o.lat))
         * SIN(RADIANS(otl.lat))))))*1000) < 200
  GROUP BY 1{code}

*TLDR;* Phone masking for call between rider ↔︎ driver can potentially break.

----

# Rider has an account with phone number A
# RB operator creates a RB ride (any ride type) with phone number A
# Rider changes the phone number from A to B
# On {{DRIVER_ON_ROUTE_TO_CLIENT}} and {{ARRIVED_AT_CLIENT}} states, we send SMS with driver’s masked phone number to A. But in RB code, we use {{rider_id}} to create the masking and hence the masking is setup with phone: B*.*
# Due to #4, the rider may call driver’s masked number from A, but the call will never be connected as the masking is created with B.

I think we can ignore this case before of rarity, what do you guys think?

----

*Conclusion:* After some discussion on Slack thread, we decided to park this concern and wait for real life complaint for it. Likely hood of Rider changing his/her phone during the active order is practically zero.

Glad you find this is useful. To answer your questions:

{quote}The {{has long_query_time=0 }}means that the slow log in fact contains all selects, DMLs and DDLs, right?{quote}

Yes, indeed all the queries will be logged to slow query log. However, pt-upgrade by default (and the way we are using it) will only run read only queries:

”By default, *pt-upgrade* only executes {{SELECT}} and {{SET}} statements. (This does not include ‘SELECT…INTO’ statements, which do not return rows but dump output to a file or variable.) If you’re using recreatable test or development servers and wish to compare write statements too (e.g. {{INSERT}}, {{UPDATE}}, {{DELETE}}), then specify {{--no-read-only}}.”
[https://docs.percona.com/percona-toolkit/pt-upgrade.html#read-only|https://docs.percona.com/percona-toolkit/pt-upgrade.html#read-only|smart-link] 



{quote}*If* we would run the pt-upgrade tool with the replication enabled{quote}

We don’t consider this scenario. We are only considering running pt-upgrade against a stop replica of MySQL and TiDB without traffic on tested schema. The “query time” metric will be present in the report.

{quote}[3] In live is the COMMERCE cluster running (as of now) only one schema (taxify_payment_order) productively, that’s in use by low-volume service without APIs, that only executes crons and processes notifications. Imo we could use the COMMERCE cluster for taxify_payment related testing.{quote}

I spoke with team and we agree that we can do this one off scenario (testing on LIVE) given the conditions you mention above (COMMERCE is a new cluster with very little live traffic). In normal situations, testing would need to be on PRELIVE.
