Hey Roberto! 👋 My apologies for a late update on this ticket, I’m a bit swamped with Rides related requests. 

I investigated the cases you shared together with the Identity team and these were the findings:

* Example 1 - [Beehive case|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/206639667], [driver lead application|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/driver-registration/driverRegistrations/edit/17140082?filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A25%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%7D%7D&tz=Europe%2FTallinn&tab=details], [the existing driver profile|https://admin.bolt.eu/fleet/Drivers/driver/4250119], reported in April 10th
** The reported driver account was ID-verified and the document matches the one in the case. It’s all one person, so there’s no identity theft.
* Example 2 - [Beehive case|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/211596325], [driver lead application|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/driver-registration/driverRegistrations/edit/17009110?filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A25%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%7D%7D&tz=America%2FAsuncion&tab=details], [the existing driver profile|https://admin.bolt.eu/fleet/Drivers/driver/1899763], reported in April 21st
** There was never any identity verification for this one, and the partner account was blocked before we rolled out identity verification, on 2022-09-28.
* Example 3 - [Beehive case|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/198844816], [driver profile|https://admin.bolt.eu/fleet/Drivers/driver/2734221], reported in March 24th
** The driver account evaded identity verification.

The above cases don’t showcase identity theft. Additionally, there are two types of verification enabled for the Paraguay market (driving licence verification and the driver selfie check), so cases of identity theft technically shouldn’t happen. 

In case such cases are reported, you may verify the user - but not by asking for a selfie with an ID document and date, but by using the [user identity verification method via Veriff|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360018988839]. 

As for the process, the case examples provided don’t warrant any CS process updates yet. With that said, I’ll close the ticket. If you observe an increase in such cases, please share relevant data showcasing the increase and we’ll take a second look into the examples and the potential CS process update(s). 🙂

Hey Alexandra! 👋 

Handling situations like this (where the rider insists on their own truth despite what our investigation uncovered) doesn’t require a CS process change. Essentially, this can be any issue - not just the ride not happening - where the user can disagree with our investigation findings and the corresponding actions on our side. With that said, this is more of a matter of skills (how to handle when users disagree with the investigation findings and the proposed solution).

In this case, the rider disagrees with us saying that we cannot confirm that the ride actually happened. The rider’s preferred outcome is likely compensation. We can:

* try explaining to the rider why our actions are limited (which means re-wording what was already said - but not by repeating what has already been said in previous agent messages, which may be taken negatively by the user) or
* issue a courtesy compensation (if the current compensation guidelines allow so - but the key is to make it clear that this is a courtesy compensation where we normally don’t issue them).

I’m not sure how often riders in such a situation would be able to provide proof of other kinds of transportation they used (they may or may not have done so). Regardless, it’s even more friction for an already frustrated user, so my recommendation would be to either inform the user or issue a courtesy compensation if it’s allowed.

Hi [~accountid:5cfe57d9a7095c0c3ffac38d] as discussed, I’m updating and addressing your feedback:

* *Problem statement:* When it comes to process efficiency Imo a problem statement should be “The current _metric_ is this, and we want it to be that” or “The processes are not effective because it takes a lot of time for agents to solve cases that they should solve in x amount of time, and we know this because we have a benchmark”. Instead, the reality is that “We want to make processes *more* efficient”, but we don’t have a standard. At this point, the processes could actually be efficient (hence no hypothesis that those are not), but we want them to be even *more*. In short, no data, no benchmark, no standard → continuous improvement, no problem statement.
* *“No issue found in the list”:* This is just the high-level goal. I’ve added a bit more context, however more details, data, etc are in the attached task 👌 
* *Progressive approach:* This means that I will not commit to any statement that says “Top 3/5/10 issues”. Before reaching the 8th, 9th or any issue in the list, we should start from the top, with the most impactful, until we realise we either cannot do anything about it and it’s always going to be top issue (not just because of the volume), or it drops and we can focus on the next big issue. There is no point in talking about a certain top of issues without actually fixing anything. Otherwise, we risk reviewing and “optimising” a lot of different things with no clear focus.
* *“Is top issue review an outcome on its own”:* I am not 100% sure if it’s outcome or deliverable or both. Considering that at the moment, there isn't any supporting data / hypothesis to begin with and this is something that I have to map myself and dig for the data, an initial picture of CS process health/metrics would be paramount for actual progress. 
* *Efficiency as deliverable:* True, this is an outcome. Ive removed it from that section.
* *Success metrics:* I’ve added your suggestions.

I guess it is mostly device-related.  The app that is using microphone should release it. Since we dont get any callback that the microphone is in use or not as per system behavior, we are not handling interruption cases. We are letting the timer run. But on the other hand, Media recorder that we use in our app will only have access to this information and record at a point it gets access to microphone resource. I think it would be ok to stop recording when any interruptions happen for the first cut as it is a restricted system behaviour and as long as privacy is not breached.

Reference:
[https://stackoverflow.com/questions/24170124/unable-to-access-microphone-when-another-app-is-using-it-in-android|https://stackoverflow.com/questions/24170124/unable-to-access-microphone-when-another-app-is-using-it-in-android|smart-link] 
From the above link

{quote}Sadly,
*only one app at a time can access the microphone* (just like the camera).
Also, there is no standard way to inform another app that you want access to the microphone (so that they release the resources and let you access it). You could however send a broadcast to all other apps (“requesting the microphone”), but the other apps would have to implement this feature (and very few or zero developers will do this).
I would recommend you to *simply inform the user* that the microphone is currently not available, because you can’t do anything else.{quote}

We need to investigate further for a generic solution so it does not affect default behavior and also does not break any other case using a microphone

The prosecutor contacted Ahto and that’s what they answered:

_Tere_

_Leppisime eile telefoni teel kokku, et saadan teile uurimisasutuse poolt edastatud päringu. Tänan teid juba ette võimaliku abi eest!_

_Teie ettevõttest saabunud keeldumisest nähtub, et lähtutakse isikuandmete kaitse ülddirektiivist, millega sätestati üldised normid füüsiliste isikute kaitseks isikuandmete töötlemisel ning isikuandmete vaba liikumise tagamiseks liidus (Euroopa Parlamendi ja nõukogu määrus (EL) 2016/679). Käesoleval juhul on päring esitatud Eesti Vabariigis Eesti Vabariigi ettevõttele ning mitte mingit andmete liigutamist liikmesriikide vahel ei toimu. Lisaks on tegemist päringuga kriminaalmenetluses, mis tähendab, et kohalduks hoopiski erinormid, mis käsitlevad füüsiliste isikute kaitset seoses pädevates asutustes isikuandmete töötlemisega süütegude tõkestamise, uurimise, avastamise ja nende eest vastutusele võtmise või kriminaalkaristuste täitmisele pööramise, sealhulgas avalikku julgeolekut ähvardavate ohtude eest kaitsmise ja nende ennetamise eesmärgil (Euroopa Parlamendi ja Nõukogu direktiiv (EL) 2016/680)._

_Küll aga on antud juhul olukord veelgi lihtsam. Uurimisasutusel on õigus esitada nõudeid ning nende täitmine on kohustuslik. Tegemist on päringuga, millel jaoks pole ka vaja kohtu luba. See, kas päringu maht on proportsionaalne ja vajalik, selle üle otsustab menetlust juhtiv prokurör, s.o mina._

_Bolt Operations OÜ on taotlenud ka andmete avaldamist (soovite teada, millist kuritegu uurime). Annan teada, et tegemist on I astme kuriteoga (karistused üle viie aasta vangistuse) ning sellega ka käesolevas menetlusetapis pean piirduma. Konspireeritud kuritegude tõkestamine, avastamine ja tõendite kogumine on niivõrd keerukas tänapäevasel tehnoloogiaajastul, et igasugune infoleke võib kriminaalmenetluse tõsisesse ohtu seada. Sellest tulenevalt ei ole käesolevas menetlusetapis võimalik lisaandmeid esitada._

_Ma oskan vaid oletada, et keeldumise põhjuseks võivad olla välisriikidest saabuvad märksa mahukama sisuga taotlused. Välisriigid ongi sunnitud rohkem avaldama, sest nemad loodavad vabatahtlikule koostööle, kuivõrd otsepäringute korral ei ole päringule vastamisel kohustust. Tegemist on vabatahtliku koostööga, mida tõsi küll, väga erinevad ettevõtted harrastavad. Aga sellisel juhul on neil võimalus sättida kriteeriume, sest nad tegutsevad vaba tahte alusel. Sellist võimalust siseriiklikult pole, sest siin kohalduvad kehtestatud seadused ja peab lähtuma neist. Nii näiteks, kui Eesti uurimisasutus pöördub Facebooki poole, siis me ka väga alandlikult täidame kõiki nende nõudmisi, sest loodame nende lahkele vabatahtlikule koostööle. Oleks tegemist Eestis registreeritud ettevõttega, siis saaksime samamoodi viidata kriminaalmenetluse seadustikule._

_Ma loodan, et minu selgitused on selged ja piisavad ja väga loodan, et Bolt Operations OÜ seaduskuuleka isikuna annab oma hindamatu panuse kuritegevusvastaseks võitluseks Eestis. Meie omalt poolt kinnitame, et päringud on alati läbimõeldud ja põhjendatud ning järgivad kõiki seadustes sätestatud nõudeid._

_Kirja manuses on uurija kirjavahetus teie kolleegiga ning ka vastuseta jäänud päring._

{noformat}def assumption_plot(df, target_var, counterfactual_var, interrupted_variable, intervention, post_window = 15, pre_window = 60, figsize = (25,10)):

    dataframe = df.copy()
    condition_range = (dataframe.ds >= pd.to_datetime(intervention[0]) - pd.Timedelta(days=pre_window))&(dataframe.ds <= pd.to_datetime(intervention[1]) + pd.Timedelta(days=post_window))
    
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(nrows = 4, ncols = 1, figsize = figsize)
    fig.subplots_adjust(wspace=0.8)

    lineplot = dataframe[condition_range].set_index('ds')[target_var].plot(color = 'green', ax=axes[0],alpha=.9)

    dataframe[condition_range].set_index('ds')[counterfactual_var].plot(color = 'orange', ax=axes[0], linestyle='--',alpha=.9)
    
    lineplot.axvline(pd.to_datetime(intervention[0]), color='red', linestyle='--', alpha=.5)
    lineplot.legend([target_var, counterfactual_var])
    axes[0].set_title(f'Counterfactual relationship with the target')

#Glossary

###DataFrame Objetcs:
- `df_main`: DataFrame which contains the main query results to measurement libraries.
- `df`: Copy of 'df_main'.
- `df_int_var`: DataFrame which contains only the interrupted variable during the whole period and grouped by day.
- `ts_[breakdown]_[metric]`: DataFrame which is grouped by day and each control variable as column, where the values are the metric analyzed.
- `df_temp`: DataFrame which is a copy of **ts_**. usually filtered by only the needed columns and the one used on the final analysis.

###Functions:
- `running_job`: Used to return a Pandas DataFrame from a query.
- `pivot_dataframe`: Used to transform the dataframe and return rows as columns.
- `mean_absolute_percentage_error`:
- `normalize_variables`: 
- `assumption_plot`: Plot a picture showing the relationship between control variables and target, in addition to the change on the interrupted variable.
- `model_validation`: Used to return a DataFrame which shows a power analysis based on the model selected on Causal Impact.
- `model_evaluation_plot`: Used to return a plot of the model detection for each fake effect.
- `ci_plot`: Used to plot the results from Causal Impact.
- `linear_incremental_effect`: Return how much the linear incremental on A represents on B.
- `create_pdf`: Create an PDF overview saved on S3.{noformat}

Statistics

2.695.144 - Number of drivers known to the work time system in the driver_work_time_check table.

            This is the number of driver who have been online at least once since we implemented the system.

            They are continuously checked over and over again. That seems to be a waste.

693.852 - Number of drivers online in the last 7 days

347.060 - Number of drivers online in the last 7 days with an active work time configuration in their city

Only keeping driver_work_time_check for drivers who were online in the last 7 days and have an active work time configuration in their city, will shrink the driver_work_time_check table size to 12.9% of its current size.

This seems a good optimization as we add back driver_work_time_check rows when a driver starts working.

Therefore, the proposal is not creating a compliance gap.

Implementation

 :one: Change to the event listener

 Only create a driver_work_time_check row for drivers if there is an active configuration in their city.

 :two: Write a clean-up cron that keeps looping over all driver_work_time_check rows.

 Delete the row, if

there is no active configuration for the driver’s city.

the driver wasn’t working in the last 7 days (i.e. the driver_state_log_X table does not contain any rows for this driver)

If the above is not enough

:three: Remove the “WHERE city_id IN (...)” clause from the accumulating check cron’s.

Skip a row in the cron if the driver does not have an active accumulating configuration in their city.

This seems a good optimization since there are no cities with an active rolling configuration.{quote}

Hi! Correct me if I am wrong, but from my understanding the age verification was requested only by the insurance company. The law does prescribe that minors and people without driving license are not permitted to drive scooters, but it says nothing about us being obliged to verify that. 

The regulation prescribes the following: 

Operators of shared fleets are responsible *to program their technological framework in such a way as to put into effect all such parts of the regulatory framework which may be implemented into the body of its technological framewor*k. 

*Operators of shared e-kickscooter fleets shall inform and/or advise users of their fleet with the necessary information, instruction and advice that is contained within the regulations through the same web-based application that is used to provide their service*. A summary containing all the main points of the regulations shall be made available on their web-based application and shall be updated to reflect any and all amendments and/ or updates to the said regulations. 

 It shall not be lawful for any person to use or to cause or permit any other person to use an e-kickscooter on the road unless there is in force in relation to the user of the e-kickscooter by that person or that other person, as the case may be, such a policy of insurance in respect of third-party risks as complies with the requirements of the Motor Vehicles Insurance (Third Party Risks) Ordinance, Cap . 104 of the Laws of Malta requirement applies both to private users as well as to e-kickscooter sharing operations. 

*E-kickscooter users shall be in possession of a valid driving licence under Category A, B or AM (from 18 years upwards) to drive on public roads. Riders must carry their driving licence on their person whilst using an e-kickscooter.* 

Users driving an e-kickscooter without a valid driving licence will be liable to a fine (multa) of not more than €1,000 or to imprisonment up to 1 year. {color:#bf2600}*The same penalties also apply to whomever permits any other person to drive an e-kickscooter without a licence.*{color}



Therefore, I think that we can be fined in case we allow riders to use e-scooters without driver’s license. We could maybe sent an alert before they start their ride and warn them that they need to have a driving license, otherwise they are fully liable for all the concequences, however I do not know if, according to the relevant authorities, that would be sufficient proof that we did everything we could to prevent them from breaching the law.

{code:sql}WITH abusers AS (
SELECT 
k.driver AS driver_id,
k.city_id AS city_id,
COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN k.pattern1 = 1 THEN k.order_id END) AS destination_cancellations,
COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN k.driver_rejection = 1 THEN k.order_id END) AS count_driver_rejections,
COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN k.pattern1 = 1 THEN k.order_id END)*1.00 / COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN k.driver_rejection = 1 THEN k.order_id END) AS ratio_destination_cancellations_in_all_rejections  -- against valid rejections 
FROM (
SELECT DISTINCT 
o.id AS order_id, 
o.created AS order_created,  
otl.city_id AS city_id,
o.country AS country,
ot.driver_id AS driver,
CASE WHEN o.state = 'no_driver_provided' AND ot.state = 'driver_rejected' AND otl.to_state = 'driver_rejected' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS driver_rejection,
CASE WHEN o.state = 'no_driver_provided' AND ot.state = 'driver_rejected' AND otl.from_state = 'driver_accepted' AND otl.to_state = 'driver_rejected' AND (DATEDIFF(minute, o.created, otl.created) >= ot.time_to_client_estimate) AND ROUND((111.111 *
    DEGREES(ACOS(LEAST(1.0, COS(RADIANS(o.lat))
         * COS(RADIANS(otl.lat))
         * COS(RADIANS(o.lng - otl.lng))
         + SIN(RADIANS(o.lat))
         * SIN(RADIANS(otl.lat))))))*1000) < 200 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS pattern1
FROM 
ng_public_spark.company_order AS o
JOIN ng_public_spark.company_order_try as ot ON ot.city_id = o.city_id AND o.id=ot.order_id 
JOIN ng_public_spark.company_order_try_state_log as otl ON otl.city_id = ot.city_id AND otl.order_try_id = ot.id
WHERE 
o.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
AND ot.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
AND otl.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE) 
AND o.state = 'no_driver_provided' AND ot.state = 'driver_rejected' AND otl.to_state = 'driver_rejected'
) AS k 
GROUP BY 1,2 
HAVING 
COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN k.pattern1 = 1 THEN k.order_id END) > 10 
AND 
COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN k.pattern1 = 1 THEN k.order_id END)*1.00 / COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN k.driver_rejection = 1 THEN k.order_id END) >= 0.6
) 
SELECT 
o.city_id || ':' || o.id AS KEY,
1 as offline_ride_pickup_cancellation
FROM 
ng_public_spark.company_order AS o
JOIN ng_public_spark.company_order_try as ot ON ot.city_id = o.city_id AND o.id=ot.order_id 
JOIN abusers AS a ON a.driver_id = ot.driver_id 
JOIN ng_public_spark.company_order_try_state_log as otl ON otl.city_id = ot.city_id AND otl.order_try_id = ot.id
WHERE 
o.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
AND ot.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
AND otl.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)

    DEGREES(ACOS(LEAST(1.0, COS(RADIANS(o.lat))
         * COS(RADIANS(otl.lat))
         * COS(RADIANS(o.lng - otl.lng))
         + SIN(RADIANS(o.lat))
         * SIN(RADIANS(otl.lat))))))*1000) < 200

{quote}*1.* We need to know how the existing selfie verification scheduling works for Riders{quote}

Every time a user creates an order {{trip-safety}} {{/internal/checkRider}} endpoint is called down the line.

The logic there works the following way:

* Targeting response is checked
** If verification IS NOT enabled:
*** Note about check result is logged and default response is returned (i.e. “No need to verify”)
** If verification is enabled:
*** “No need to verify” response is returned if rider has already verified themselves once
*** Otherwise model-invoker is called (i.e. some model is checked).
**** NOTE: This is an optional dependency. It means rider will not need to verify themselves should the call fail for any reason.
*** If model predicts trouble then verification is requested (depending on targeting params options are either only “card verification” or both, “card verification” and “selfie verification”).



In case verification is needed, backend will throw an error and mobile side handles it by presenting a view for verification. Only one verification option must be completed.

{quote}*2.* How the Rider app handles it, which app state, such as before ordering anything or when they log in?{quote}

Verification view will be presented after rider has created an order.

{quote}*3.* Which endpoints and events do they use to schedule for Riders? I&T has the verification framework. {quote}

There’s no scheduling, only model is checked. The check happens after rider has created an order.

[~accountid:5cfe57d9a7095c0c3ffac38d] I realised some edits I’ve made to the description didnt save 😶 

* *Problem statement:* We don’t have a problem to solve. We just want to _improve_ things. At most, the hypothesis could be “processes can be improved / more efficient”. However, this is *not* a problem. If there is a problem there should be data to support it, or the other way around. There is none. Maybe I should remove the “Problem statement” section if it’s confusing.
* *Progressive approach:* I cannot commit to top 10 issues because it’s a bad approach. I never personally agreed/committed to this and we even [discussed|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C04P6E0AW86/p1682426970718219?thread_ts=1681978350.207739&cid=C04P6E0AW86] about it. Let’s say I do and then after some time I magically improve the top 10 issues. Does the work stop? No. Then it doesn't make any sense to pick a top for the sake of picking a top of issues. If this _approach_ for some reason works for anyone else, that’s fine, but it’s a fake commitment. When you mention planning, if it’s my planning, then my approach helps me more. If it’s about another type of planning, please let me know what kind of help is needed.

Top 10 approach:

*  We look at top 10 *most frequent user issues* (issues from user’s POV) and we try to *find* *process issues* to solve.

My approach:

*  I look at the *most frequent user issues* and I try to make it more efficient (saving time for agents). - _excluding no issue found in the list, as it’s a different kind of process_
* I look at a combination of the highest AHT and a significant ticket volume and based on that pick the priority for that moment. It can be the 1st, it can be the 4th most frequent *user issue*
* Either way, I will still obviously review most of the processes but not in a specific order and not a specific number. The priority of that I will decide based on data and my own research. Otherwise, I need clear expectations and a clear business case (aka supporting data) that I should be focusing on a specific process.
* In short, I will go for the “biggest problem” (not necessarily from the volumes POV) until I am confident (and proven with data) that it’s not the biggest problem anymore and I can move to the next one. Not only this helps me plan and focus but will be the most impactful approach.

I stick by this and I am happy to share more context if it’s needed. I hope you agree that there is no bulletproof plan and it can still be adapted on the way, just that I will not commit to any unrealistic standards.
